title: Assertion set
description: Every relational fact in the ontology is a first-class, provenanced, confidence-scored assertion. This is the hook for machine learning: a model may add candidates with status 'proposed', a curator promotes or rejects them, and reviewed assertions become the training set for the next model.

object.description: Entity or concept ID. Mutually exclusive with 'value'.

value.description: Literal object, for predicates whose range is a literal.

status.description: Only 'asserted' is published to the portal. 'proposed' is a model or rule candidate awaiting review. 'rejected' is a negative label and is kept, because negatives are as valuable to training as positives.

method.description: Free-text method tag, e.g. source-metadata, lexical-rule, tfidf-knn, logistic-regression, curator.

evidence.description: Why this assertion exists. Rules record matched terms; models record features, neighbours and scores. Required for anything not taken verbatim from the source metadata.
